subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Stress Management, Mental Skills, and Movement

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of movement as a regulation tool and its realistic limits in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe attention, arousal, and performance under pressure using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply routines, breathing, and refocusing techniques in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving motivation, discipline, and what to do when both are gone; correct it and explain why.
Connect the difference between healthy commitment and compulsive activity with when a difficulty needs support beyond movement and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Build a movement-and-regulation toolkit with a routine for a good week, a routine for a hard week, and a written statement of when the learner would seek support beyond movement.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Stress Management, Mental Skills, and Movement?
